title: How to open the command menu in Linear on Mac with the ⌘K shortcut
metaTitle: How to Open the Command Menu in Linear on Mac (⌘K)
description: How to open the command menu in Linear on Mac: select an issue, press ⌘K, and fix it when the shortcut does nothing. Steps for the desktop app.

intro: To open the command menu in Linear on Mac, select an issue, then press ⌘K, which is Command and K together. Linear's docs call it the command bar, and its changelog calls it the command menu, so you may see either name.
tldr: Select an issue first. Highlight it and press X, or Shift+click it.
Then press ⌘K, which is Command and K together, to open the command menu.
Linear's docs call it the command bar. The changelog calls it the command menu.
Right-click the selected issue if you want a contextual menu with similar actions.
If ⌘K does nothing, check the focus, the selection and the browser you are using.

blocks.text: The short answer for Linear on Mac

Here is the full routine. Open the Linear desktop app, select one or more issues, then press Command and K together. The command menu opens, and the actions it shows apply to the issues you selected. Linear's documentation says this in plain terms: once an issue or set of issues is selected, use Cmd or Ctrl K to open the command bar. On a Mac, the shortcut is Cmd K, which is the ⌘K you see in menus and guides.
Select a single issue or a range first

The docs only describe the shortcut after a selection, so treat the selection as the first step every time. Linear gives two ways to select a single issue. You can highlight the issue and press X, or you can Shift+click it. Both routes leave the issue selected for the shortcut that follows.

To extend a range, hold Shift after selecting the first issue, then use the up and down arrow keys. Press Esc when you want to clear the selection and start again. Range selection helps with batch work, but it has a trap, covered in the note below.

blocks.title: Filter before you press Command A
blocks.text: Command A selects every issue in the board or list you are viewing. Linear's docs advise filtering the list first. Filter, check what is selected, then open the command menu.
Search inside the command menu

Linear's changelog for 3 Sep 2026 says the command menu now uses fuzzy search. Type a few letters from the action you want, and the list narrows. You do not need the exact wording. This helps when you cannot remember the full name of an action.

The same changelog says the desktop app now uses Cmd N to choose what to create, based on the view you are in. Native creation commands now include documents. So the same shortcut can make different things in different views, which is worth checking before you press it on a new screen.
Right-click as a backup route

If the shortcut keeps failing, right-click the selected issue. Linear's docs say a right-click anywhere on the selected issue or issues opens a contextual menu with a list of available actions. It is not the same panel as the command menu. It offers similar kinds of actions, so you can often finish the same task from it.
Desktop app or browser on a Mac

Linear's download notes list the desktop app for macOS on both Intel and Apple Silicon. The desktop app also runs on Windows. Linux is not supported, and Linear says a Linux app is not on the roadmap for now, so Linux users use the browser version. On a Mac, the desktop app also brings OS notifications, unread counts in the Dock, and tabs. It installs updates automatically in the background.

blocks.text: Which Macs and macOS versions work

The desktop app runs on Intel Macs and on Apple Silicon Macs. Linear's download page does not state a minimum macOS version. The notes I checked do not give one either, so check the download page before you install. If you are on an older Mac, that check matters most.
What the Mac keyboard symbols mean

Linear writes shortcuts with Mac symbols. Apple's Mac keyboard guide names the modifier keys: Command (⌘), Option (⌥), Control (⌃), and Shift (⇧). Windows and Linux use Ctrl where Mac uses ⌘, so Ctrl K is the same action on those systems. Option is also called Alt on Windows keyboards.

blocks.caption: Mac modifier symbols and their Windows or Linux equivalents.

blocks.text: When ⌘K does nothing on Mac

Most failed attempts come from a few causes. There may be no selection, the focus may sit in a text field, or the browser may claim the key first. Apple's guide shows that Command K means different things in different apps. In one context it adds a web link. In Finder, it connects to a server. So the same two keys can do different jobs depending on where your cursor sits.
Quick checks before you retry

items: Confirm the issue is highlighted or Shift+clicked, not just under your pointer.
Click the issue list, not a title or comment box, so focus leaves the text field.
Press Esc, then select the issue again if an old selection may be in the way.
Check that you are holding Command, not Control.
Switch to the desktop app if the browser keeps taking the shortcut.

blocks.text: Ask Lazur where the command menu is

Lazur helps when you would rather ask than hunt. Hold Option and Command together, then ask out loud. Ask where the command menu is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Lazur does not press keys or click for you. You still do the work, while Lazur points the way. The Linear setup is covered on [Lazur for Linear on Mac](/apps/linear).
Mistakes that waste time
A few habits cause most of the wasted time with this shortcut. Each one is easy to fix once you spot it.

items: Pressing ⌘K before selecting anything, then guessing which issue the menu will use.
Leaving an old selection active and acting on issues you did not mean to touch.
Typing in a comment or description box, where Apple's text editing shortcuts use ⌘K to add a web link.
Pressing Control K by mistake on a Mac. Ctrl K is the Windows and Linux shortcut.

blocks.text: Build the habit in one short session

Open a filtered list. Select one issue with X, open the command menu with ⌘K, then press Esc. Repeat with a range, using Shift and the arrow keys. Then type a few letters of an action name and watch the fuzzy search narrow the list. Short practice runs are easier to repeat than a long read through a shortcut list.
What the research did not confirm

The research behind this page did not find Linear's official keyboard shortcut page, because the URL returned a 404 during research. It also did not find a Mac menu bar path for the command menu, a minimum macOS version, or a current desktop app version number. This page does not fill those gaps with guesses. If you need them, check Linear's download page or ask Linear's support team.
Where to go next

If you manage product work in Linear, [Linear for product managers on Mac](/for/product-managers/linear) covers board shortcuts, templates and plan limits. If you run triage, [Linear for software QA testers on Mac](/for/software-qa-testers/linear) covers triage, templates and shortcuts with Lazur. Start with one issue and one shortcut, then add the rest.

faq.question: Is the command menu called the command bar in Linear?
faq.answer: Yes, the two names describe the same feature. Linear's docs call it the command bar, and its changelog calls it the command menu. Both open with ⌘K on a Mac after you select an issue.

faq.question: Do I have to select an issue before pressing ⌘K?
faq.answer: The docs describe the shortcut after a selection, so select first. Highlight an issue and press X, or Shift+click it. Then press ⌘K.

faq.question: Why does ⌘K do nothing in my browser?
faq.answer: The browser or the focused text field may use ⌘K for something else. Apple's guide shows that Command K adds a web link in some text editing contexts. Linear says its desktop shortcuts are less likely to conflict with browser shortcuts, so try the desktop app.

faq.question: Does the Linear desktop app work on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Yes. Linear's docs list the desktop app for macOS on Intel and on Apple Silicon. The download page does not state a minimum macOS version, so check it before you install.

faq.question: Can I use Linear's command menu on Linux?
faq.answer: Not with the desktop app. Linear says it does not support Linux and that a Linux app is not on the roadmap for now. Linux users use the browser version, on one of the three most recent versions of Chrome, Firefox or Safari.

faq.question: What does fuzzy search change in the command menu?
faq.answer: Since the 3 Sep 2026 changelog, you can type part of an action name without the exact wording. The list narrows to matches. Use it when you cannot remember the full name of an action.

faq.question: Does Lazur open the command menu for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate Linear for you. Ask it where the command menu is and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something and it guides you one click at a time.

faq.question: Where is the Mac menu bar item for the command menu?
faq.answer: The docs I checked do not list a menu bar item for it, so this page does not give a menu path. Use the keyboard shortcut, or right-click the selected issue instead.

steps.name: Open the issue list or board
steps.text: Open the Linear desktop app on your Mac. Go to the team, view or project that holds the issue you want. Filter the list first if you plan to select many issues.

steps.name: Select the issue
steps.text: Highlight the issue, then press X. You can also Shift+click the issue. Either way, the issue is selected and ready for an action.

steps.name: Press ⌘K
steps.text: Hold Command and press K. Linear calls this the command bar in its docs, and the command menu in its changelog. Both names refer to the same set of actions.

steps.name: Type to find an action
steps.text: Type a few letters of the action you want. Since 3 Sep 2026, the menu uses fuzzy search, so you do not need the exact wording. Pick the action from the narrowed list.
steps.tip: Partial words work, so a short fragment is often faster than scrolling.

steps.name: Clear the selection
steps.text: Press Esc to clear the selection when you finish. Clearing it first helps you avoid acting on issues you did not mean to touch.

steps.name: Use right-click if the shortcut fails
steps.text: Right-click anywhere on the selected issue. Linear opens a contextual menu with a list of available actions. Use it when the keyboard route does not work for you.

troubleshooting.fix: Confirm an issue is selected first. Highlight the issue and press X, or Shift+click it, then press ⌘K again.

troubleshooting.problem: ⌘K adds a link or does something else
troubleshooting.fix: Your cursor is probably in a text field. Apple's text editing shortcuts use Command K to add a web link. Click an issue row to move focus out of the field, then press ⌘K.
Linear says its desktop shortcuts are less likely to conflict with browser shortcuts. Try the Linear desktop app on your Mac.
An old selection may still be active. Press Esc to clear it, then select again and check the highlight before you open the menu.

troubleshooting.problem: Control K does nothing on a Mac
troubleshooting.fix: You may be pressing Control K. Ctrl K is the Windows and Linux shortcut. On a Mac, use Command K.

troubleshooting.problem: A Linux user cannot find the desktop app
troubleshooting.fix: Linear does not support Linux for its desktop app. Use the browser version, on one of the three most recent versions of Chrome, Firefox or Safari.
